about.text: Acid-set or sour milk cheese is cheese that has been curdled (coagulated) by natural souring, often from lactic acid bacteria, or by the addition of acid. This type of cheese is technologically simple to produce.

how.text: Yeasts eat the lactic acid on the surface of the quark loaf and raise its pH; only then can the smear bacteria grow and give the yellow or red rind and strong smell.

steps.note: Sodium bicarbonate (Natron) or calcium carbonate, to neutralise part of the acid.
steps.what: salt, spices (caraway) and a ripening agent

steps.note: Sweated a few days, warm and very humid, the film yeasts coming first.
Smeared with salted water and red cultures.
Kept cooler a few more days.

processing.text: The quark is soured within a few hours, then sweated a few days warm and very humid, smeared with salted water and red cultures and kept cooler a few more days. Mould sorts are ripened 6-7 days at 17-19 °C.

facts.v: For white or blue mould sorts the quark is salted less and neutralised less, with no sweating; ripened 6–7 days at 17–19 °C
